question.problem:
The function $f(x)$ is given by

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{\sqrt{x+k}-\sqrt{k}}, & x\ne 0, \\ 18, & x=0.\end{aligned}
$$

If $f(x)$ is continuous at $x=0$, what is the value of $k?$
question.worked_solution:
From the definition of $f(x),$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 0}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{x}{\sqrt{x+k}-\sqrt{k}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}(\frac{x}{\sqrt{x+k}-\sqrt{k}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{x+k}+\sqrt{k}}{\sqrt{x+k}+\sqrt{k}}) \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{x(\sqrt{x+k}+\sqrt{k})}{x+k-k} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{\cancel{x}(\sqrt{x+k}+\sqrt{k})}{\cancel{x}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}(\sqrt{x+k}+\sqrt{k}) \\  & =\sqrt{0+k}+\sqrt{k} \\  & =2\sqrt{k}.\end{aligned}
$$

In order for $f(x)$ to be continuous at $x=0,$ we must have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 0}f(x) & =f(0) \\ 2\sqrt{k} & =18 \\ \sqrt{k} & =9 \\ k & =81.\end{aligned}
$$
